How is juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) defined?
Arthritis that starts before 16 years of age and lasts 6 weeks or more, after other causes are excluded.
When does a joint have arthritis?
When it is swollen, or has two of: limited movement, pain on movement and warmth.
How do young children with arthritis usually present?
Limp, morning stiffness or not using a limb (rarely pain).

Which subtype of juvenile idiopathic arthritis has the worst joint outcome?

What is the fever pattern of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis?
Quotidian fever: one or two spikes a day, normal between them, for 2 weeks or more.
What is the rash of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis?
An evanescent salmon-pink rash that comes with the fever.

What are the features of psoriatic juvenile idiopathic arthritis?
Dactylitis, nail pitting, and psoriasis in the child or a first-degree relative.
Is there a diagnostic test for juvenile idiopathic arthritis?
No; it is a clinical diagnosis of exclusion.
What must be excluded before systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis is diagnosed?
Leukaemia (blood film and bone marrow), kala-azar, tuberculosis and systemic lupus erythematosus.
What is the use of the ANA in juvenile idiopathic arthritis?
It predicts the risk of uveitis.
What is the use of rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP in juvenile idiopathic arthritis?

What happens to the ESR in macrophage activation syndrome?
It falls (fibrinogen is consumed) while the fever persists.
What is the laboratory picture of macrophage activation syndrome?
Falling platelets and white cells, a very high ferritin, high triglycerides and a low fibrinogen.
How is macrophage activation syndrome treated?
With intravenous methylprednisolone and ciclosporin or anakinra.

What is the first-line disease-modifying drug in juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and its dose?
Methotrexate 10–15 mg/m² once weekly, with folic acid.
What is monitored during methotrexate treatment?
The complete blood count and liver tests every 1–3 months.

When are oral steroids used in juvenile idiopathic arthritis?
In systemic disease with serositis or macrophage activation syndrome, or as a short bridge.
When is treatment stepped up to a biological agent?
